sections.h2: Who runs property tax billing and valuation in Orange County, North Carolina?
sections.html:
Orange County Tax Administration does both. Its office is in the Gateway Center at 228 S. Churton Street, Suite 200, Hillsborough, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 8181, Hillsborough, NC 27278-8181.

Call 919-245-2100 or write to tax@orangecountync.gov. The Revenue and Collections division bills property tax and ambulance fees, and its counter serves weekdays until 5 p.m. A drop box outside the building takes checks and money orders but never cash.

  • Valuation, listing and appeals: Tax Administration, Suite 200
  • Bills and payment: Revenue and Collections, same suite
  • Phone payment line for cards: 919-583-6137
  • Mobile option: the MyOrangeCountyNC app for bills and scheduled payments

sections.h2: When was Orange County last revalued and when is the next revaluation?
sections.html:
The latest countywide revaluation is dated January 1, 2025, the one before it January 1, 2021, and the county's page names January 1, 2029 for the next.

Four years between revaluations is shorter than the state's eight-year ceiling, which lets a county pick a quicker cycle. Appraisers used market sales, building costs and income and expense data to estimate what each parcel would have sold for on the effective date. The county calls this mass appraisal. It is no inspection of individual homes. Until 2029 your value stays pegged to January 1, 2025, whatever the market does in between.

The county's revaluation page offers owners a property record card search, a comparable-sales tool, the 2025 schedule of values, a sales bank, a heat map of percent increases and a map of appraisal neighborhoods. Pulling up your neighborhood before you list helps you judge whether the assessment is near a likely sale price.

sections.h2: What tax rates apply in Orange County?
sections.html:
It depends on where the house sits. Each parcel carries a rate code that stacks the county tax with any city, fire district and school special district taxes.

The county's rate page shows combined rates for the 2026 tax year per one dollar of value and says they are updated each July. Call 919-245-2100 to confirm what applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an Orange County property value?
sections.html:
The county describes three steps. A county appraiser handles the informal review first, a citizen board hears formal appeals next, and the state Property Tax Commission is an optional third stop. Filing with the county costs nothing and a lawyer is optional.

The 2026 dates have passed. For 2026, informal requests were open January 1 to March 31, the board met starting April 30, and formal filings closed June 30. The county publishes new dates each year on its appeals page, so check there before planning a filing.

  • The owner has to prove the value is off from market on January 1, 2025, or out of step with comparable parcels.
  • The percentage of increase and your ability to pay are not grounds for a change.
  • Useful evidence includes comparable sales near January 1, 2025, appraisals from that period, closing statements, photos and repair estimates.
  • A state appeal is due 30 days after the board's letter.

You can file through the online portal, by email to Reval@orangecountync.gov, by mail to P.O. Box 8181, or in person at 228 S. Churton Street.

sections.h2: What must Orange County owners list each January?
sections.html:
Owners list personal property every year and report changes to their land or buildings. The county's listing deadline is January 31, and a late filing draws a 10% penalty.

Real property stays on the books once listed, so you only return the form when you built, added on or removed a structure. Personal property that must be listed includes manufactured homes, boats, aircraft, unlicensed vehicles and the appliances or furnishings you supply in a rental. Licensed vehicles with an annual registration are not listed. Do not enclose a tax payment with the form. Pay separately using the bill instructions.

sections.h2: What tax relief can an Orange County homeowner apply for?
sections.html:
Orange County administers three state programs, the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferment. It also points to present use value, exempt property, a builder property tax exclusion and help with the solid waste fee.

  • For tax year 2026 the state's income ceiling is $38,800. The disabled veteran program shields the first $45,000 of value.
  • The elderly or disabled program shields $25,000 or half the value of a primary home, whichever is larger.
  • The circuit breaker limits the bill to a slice of income and parks the remainder as a deferred lien.

An owner may use only one program. The county's evaluator tool on its relief page gives a quick read on which one fits, but you may skip it and just file the application with the Tax Office.

sections.h2: How and when are Orange County property taxes paid?
sections.html:
Bills fall due September 1. Interest begins January 6 under state rules, so any payment in the fall and early winter avoids it.

Payment channels are the website, the phone line, a mailed check made out to Orange County Tax Collector, the drop box and the counter, where Apple Pay and Google Pay also work. For a bill of $100 or more, five coupons let you pay in equal parts on the last day of each month, usually August to December. Other options include a pre-payment program that builds toward an estimated bill, a bank draft program and a post-billing plan. Card payments may add a convenience fee, and the county warns that it never asks for gift cards.

sections.h2: What if you sell an Orange County house with tax still owed?
sections.html:
The tax stays with the parcel, so it is paid out of proceeds at closing. Get the balance and any delinquent amount from the Tax Office first.

Your closing attorney will usually pay it directly. The seller also covers the deed stamp tax at the Register of Deeds. If you cannot cover the bill, call 919-245-2100 (Option 2) and ask about the payment assistance programs before the account goes delinquent.

sections.h2: What does Orange County look like in the census numbers?
sections.html:
The July 2025 estimate counts 152,498 people in Orange County, up 2.5% on the 2020 base, across 397.56 square miles of land. Density works out to 374 per square mile.

About 18% of residents are 65 or older. Households earn a median $90,089 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and owners with a mortgage report monthly costs near $2,221. Builders pulled 666 permits in 2025.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Orange County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay online, by calling 919-583-6137, by mail to Orange County Tax Collector at P.O. Box 8181, Hillsborough, NC 27278, at the Gateway Center drop box, or at Suite 200 of 228 S. Churton Street.

faqs.q: What is the next Orange County revaluation date?
faqs.a: The county's page gives January 1, 2029. The current values reflect the January 1, 2025 revaluation, and the previous one was January 1, 2021.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Orange County assessment this year?
faqs.a: The 2026 windows have closed. Call 919-245-2100 or email reval@orangecountync.gov to learn when the next one opens.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for a late listing in Orange County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county applies a 10% late listing penalty to personal property or property changes not listed by January 31.

faqs.q: Does a seller owe the property tax bill at closing?
faqs.a: In practice, yes. Any unpaid bill sits against the parcel, so the closing attorney normally pays it out of the seller's proceeds after the Tax Office confirms the amount.
